sentences.text: The species is known from a nearly complete skeleton including a skull found at Wawmda in Morocco's Azilal Province.
Atlasaurus is estimated to have reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of 22.5 tonnes.
The animal had a lower jaw approximately 69 cm long, a neck of 3.86 meters, a humerus of 1.95 meters, and a femur of 2 meters.
It possessed spoon-shaped teeth that featured denticles.
Unlike Brachiosaurus, Atlasaurus had a back estimated at 3.04 meters, a large skull, a short neck with at least 13 vertebrae of more uniform length, a long tail, and elongated hind limbs.
The genus name honors the Atlas Mountains in Morocco and the animal's large size, estimated at about 15 meters long.
A reconstructed tail specimen was displayed in Mexico City until it was auctioned in January 2018 to fund school rebuilding after the 2017 Puebla earthquake.
A second specimen, a near-complete tail, was discovered in Morocco and reassembled in Utah after 300 hours of preparation.
The holotype skeleton of Atlasaurus was discovered in 1981 and formally described in 1999 by Monbaron, Russell, and Taquet.
Remains were found by Monbaron, Russell, and Taquet in 1999 in the Guettioua Formation of the Atlas Mountains in Azilal Province, Morocco.
Atlasaurus had teeth shaped like spoons with serrated edges.
Recent analyses have suggested that Atlasaurus may be a member of the Turiasauria.
The most recent analysis of turiasaurs classifies Atlasaurus as a Brachiosaurid.
Atlasaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian to Callovian stages, in North Africa.
Atlasaurus lived in the middle Jurassic, approximately 165 million years ago during the Callovian stage, in what is now Africa.
The time range for Atlasaurus is estimated from 168.2 to 165.3 million years ago.
